w:r.w:t: This document is a screenshot-to-formula reference for every chart, KPI card, and table in the Company Owner Dashboard wireframe (company_owner_dashboard_wireframe.html). The wireframe uses mock data throughout; screenshots show the visual layout only. Every Formula and Data Source / Filter cell below is transcribed verbatim from the wireframe's own tooltip and drill-down text, so it can be implemented directly against a real database.

Each section pairs one dashboard screenshot with a table covering every element visible in it. Where a block has no real calculation (e.g. the Server tab's config status panel), the Formula column says so explicitly rather than inventing one.
Six top-line KPI cards visible on every login, plus three dedicated drill-down panels with unique formulas not shown elsewhere.

Six always-visible top-line metrics loaded on every admin page: total active users, overall compliance %, documents expiring in less than 30 days, documents already expired, EDS queue depth, and server disk usage.

These are the most performance-critical queries in the dashboard - every admin loads them on every page view and a stale compliance figure is the first number auditors check. Cache per IOMAD tenant with a short TTL (1-5 minutes) and aim for under 200 ms end-to-end. Any KPI below threshold must stay visually highlighted even when data is served from cache.

Each card is a single COUNT or ratio query. Compliance = valid_docs / active_users * 100 from sental_document_versions WHERE expiry_date > NOW() AND is_current=1. EDS queue: COUNT from sental_eds_log WHERE status='pending'. Disk: used_GB / total_GB * 100 from sental_server_metrics (latest collected_at per metric). All queries filtered to the current IOMAD tenant.
Grouped by IOMAD tenant. No individual names shown at this level.
sental_document_versions WHERE expiry_date > NOW() AND is_current=1
GREEN >=80% Compliant; AMBER 70-79% At risk; RED <70% Non-compliant
sental_document_versions WHERE expiry_date BETWEEN NOW() AND NOW()+30d
COUNT of documents awaiting electronic signature
OK <2 days; Urgent 2-5 days; Critical >5 days (days waiting)
Amber at 70%, Red at 90% (thresholds adjustable in Server tab)

The "Total active users" card opens a drill table (shown in this screenshot) listing Active Users and Compliance % per company, with the same formulas as above applied per-company, plus a RAG status: GREEN >=80%, AMBER 70-79%, RED <70%, BLUE = onboarding in progress. The "Expiring <30 days" and "Expired now" cards open named-employee drill lists using the identical filters listed above (no separate formula) - not screenshotted separately.
A horizontal bar chart of compliance % for every company under the tenant, sorted ascending (worst first), with a dashed reference line at 80%.

This is the central accountability view. It makes it impossible to hide a low-compliance company behind a platform-wide average. The ascending sort order (worst first) is deliberate and must never default to alphabetical - regulators review this chart during compliance audits and expect the most at-risk company to appear first.

SELECT company_name, COUNT(valid_doc_rows) / COUNT(all_user_rows) * 100 AS compliance_pct FROM sental_document_versions JOIN mdl_user ON user_id WHERE expiry_date > NOW() AND is_current=1 GROUP BY company ORDER BY compliance_pct ASC. The 80% reference line is a static UI threshold rendered by the chart component, not a database value.
users with valid docs / total active users * 100
sental_document_versions WHERE expiry_date > NOW() AND is_current=1
Sorted ascending (worst first). Reference line drawn at 80% target.
A list of documents currently awaiting electronic signature, with elapsed waiting time per document. Colour-coded: OK if waiting less than 2 days, Urgent 2-5 days, Critical more than 5 days.

Every day a document sits unsigned is a day an employee may be performing hazardous work without valid certification. The Notify All Signatories button is the primary HR intervention point for EDS delays and must trigger real transactional emails - it is not a cosmetic UI element. Failure to send these reminders is a process gap that can be cited in a safety audit.

SELECT * FROM sental_eds_log WHERE status = 'pending'. days_waiting = DATEDIFF(NOW(), sent_at). Colour threshold applied in the UI based on days_waiting value. The Notify button fires a bulk email job to all pending signers for each selected document row. Log the notify action with timestamp and triggering user for audit trail.
Days elapsed since document was sent for signature
OK: less than 2 days; Urgent: 2-5 days; Critical: more than 5 days. Notify All Signatories sends a reminder to every pending signer.
Compact capacity gauges for disk, RAM, CPU, database size, and concurrent user count - shown as an inline drill-down when clicking the Server Disk KPI card.

These five metrics cover the most common causes of LMS slowdowns and outages. Because thresholds are slider-adjustable per deployment, the implementation must read amber and red threshold values from a configuration table - never hard-code 70% or 90%. This ensures each client deployment can tune thresholds to their server specification without a code change.

SELECT metric, used, total, ROUND((used/total)*100,1) AS pct FROM sental_server_metrics WHERE collected_at = (SELECT MAX(collected_at) FROM sental_server_metrics s2 WHERE s2.metric = sental_server_metrics.metric). Compare pct against stored threshold values to determine gauge colour. Show a 7-day sparkline for each metric when clicked.
Disk / RAM / CPU / Database / Concurrent users (%)
sental_server_metrics - latest collected_at row per metric
Amber >=70%, Red >=90% (both adjustable via slider). Identical gauges also appear on the full Server tab.
Platform-wide summary combining engagement metrics, registration growth, and a per-company health roll-up.
Four platform-wide aggregate cards at the top of the Overview tab: total active users, platform uptime (last 30 days), average compliance across all companies, and active vs. total company count.

The Company Owner checks these before drilling into individual companies. Platform uptime is often contractually tracked against an SLA - a breach needs to be surfaced here proactively. Average compliance shown below the 80% target should trigger an automatic 'At Risk' label to prompt investigation.

Total users and compliance reuse KPI Strip queries without a company filter. Uptime = (total_minutes - downtime_minutes) / total_minutes * 100 from server monitoring logs (last 30 days). Active companies = COUNT(company WHERE status != 'onboarding'). Display as X / Y where X is active count and Y is total count.
Same filter as KPI Strip "Total active users"
Server monitoring logs, last 30 days (21 min downtime in example)
Same compliance formula as KPI Strip, averaged across companies
COUNT(companies with status != onboarding) / COUNT(all companies)
A stacked/grouped bar chart of new user registrations per month broken out by company, with a period selector (3 months / 1 year / 2 years / All time).

Registration growth predicts future training demand. A spike in new hires in month N creates a compliance gap risk in month N+1 if onboarding documents are not uploaded promptly. The period selector must change the SQL date range server-side - filtering a full dataset client-side will be too slow for large tenants.

SELECT DATE_FORMAT(timecreated, '%Y-%m') AS month, company_id, COUNT(*) AS new_users FROM mdl_user GROUP BY month, company_id ORDER BY month. The period selector applies WHERE timecreated >= NOW() - INTERVAL ? MONTH. Colour-code bars consistently with other company-breakdown charts.
COUNT(mdl_user WHERE timecreated falls in that month)
mdl_user.timecreated, grouped by month and by company (stacked/grouped bar). Period selector: 3 months / 1 year / 2 years / All time.

Five engagement metrics visible on the Overview tab: DAU (daily active users), MAU (monthly active users), course completion rate (last 30 days), average session length, and top-3 active courses by engagement percentage.

Low DAU or a falling completion rate is a leading indicator of future compliance failures. Employees who briefly open a course to generate a session entry but do not engage with content may still receive credit. The engagement ratio (active time / session time) catches this behaviour before it creates a regulatory risk.

DAU = COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) from login/session logs WHERE date = TODAY(). MAU = same WHERE date >= NOW() - 30 days. Completion rate = completed_enrolments / total_enrolments from course completion logs (last 30 days). Avg session = AVG(session_duration). Top-3 courses: rank by engagement % = active_time / total_session_time this month.
COUNT(DISTINCT user who logged in today)
COUNT(DISTINCT user who logged in within last 30 days)
Fire Safety L1 84%, Electrical Safety 71%, Working at Heights 52%
DAU/MAU ratio above 20% indicates healthy daily engagement (per in-app tooltip).

A roll-up table listing every company with five health columns: total users, compliance %, turnover rate, average Quilgo trust score, completion rate, and a derived status badge (Healthy / At risk / Critical / Onboarding).

This is the default landing view for the Company Owner and the most important screen in the dashboard. All five columns must be current - stale data causes incorrect escalations to client HR teams and missed compliance audits. The status badge drives how urgently a company is prioritised by the Company Owner.

All column values are already computed by other tabs - join per-company results. Badge: Healthy if compliance >= 80%, At risk if 70-79%, Critical if below 70%, Onboarding if company.status = 'onboarding'. Badge colour uses the same RAG scale as the compliance KPI. Cache the roll-up with a short TTL (1-5 min) since it aggregates many queries.
See Staff Turnover tab formula (Deactivated / Average active * 100)
See Proctoring tab (average Quilgo trust score per company)
Derived: Healthy / At risk / Critical / Onboarding, based primarily on the Compliance % threshold
Three alert cards surfacing the single worst value per category: the lowest-compliance company, the company with the most expired documents, and the server metric with the highest usage percentage.

These cards drive the first response from HR and IT admins. They must reflect live values - if stale or cached, the wrong company may be escalated or a critical server issue missed. Each card must link directly to the relevant drill-down view for immediate action. They should not use the same cache TTL as other KPIs.

No new queries needed. Run MIN(compliance_pct) over Compliance results, MAX(expired_docs_count) over Expiry results, MAX(server_metric_pct) over Server results. Surface only the single worst row per category as a clickable card. A company may appear in multiple cards if it is the worst in more than one metric.
No new formula - these surface the single worst value already computed elsewhere (lowest compliance company, highest expired-document count, highest server metric) to flag what needs attention first.
All compliance-rate views share one core formula (valid documents over active users), sliced by different dimensions.
Compliance by Company - 12-Month Trend / Snapshot / Heatmap / Expired vs Expiring / Non-Compliance by Course / Violations Table

Six views of the same compliance formula sliced by different dimensions: 12-month trend lines per company, current snapshot bars, a department x location heatmap, expired vs. expiring counts, non-compliance by course, and a filterable violations table with employee names.

Different stakeholders need different angles. HR needs the 12-month trend to detect early deterioration. Line managers need the heatmap to find which specific department or location has a problem. Each view is a different GROUP BY of the same base query - implement as parameterised variants to avoid query duplication and ensure data consistency.

Core formula: valid_docs / active_users * 100 filtered by company and time window. Heatmap: add WHERE department=? AND location=?. Trend: monthly snapshot from sental_document_versions. Violations table: JOIN to mdl_user for employee name and document details; filterable by status and doc type. Reference line at 80% on all chart views.
Dashed reference line at 80% target. A line dropping below it flags the need for HR intervention.
Same formula, current point in time
GREEN >=80; AMBER 70-79; RED <70. Sorted ascending (worst first).
valid_docs / active_users * 100, filtered to that department AND location
sental_document_versions joined to mdl_user department/location fields
RED <70%; AMBER 70-79%; GREEN >=80%. Per-company filter tabs available above the heatmap.
Status = Expired if expiry_date < NOW(), else Expiring if within 30 days
RED badge = Expired; AMBER badge = Expiring. Filterable by status/doc type, searchable by name or course.
Covers headcount change over time and the turnover-rate formula the user originally asked about.
Staff Dynamics, Turnover Rate % by Company, and New-Staff-Without-Certs Risk Panel
Three panels: a staff-dynamics bar/line chart (new hires vs. departures per month with cumulative net trend), turnover rate % per company, and a new-staff-without-certs risk panel.

Turnover above 10% is RED because it means continuous replacement of certified employees with uncertified ones. The new-staff-without-certs panel is the most safety-critical metric in this tab - an uncertified employee performing hazardous work is an immediate legal liability. Above 20% triggers a critical risk badge and must surface in the Priority Actions cards.

New hires: COUNT WHERE mdl_user.timecreated in that month. Departures: COUNT WHERE suspended or deleted flag changed in that month via timemodified. Turnover rate: departures / AVG(active headcount) * 100 over rolling 12 months. No-certs risk: COUNT(new hires with zero matching rows in sental_document_versions WHERE is_current=1) / COUNT(all new hires, last 30 days) * 100.
COUNT(mdl_user WHERE timecreated falls within that month)
Tall blue + short red = team growth
COUNT(mdl_user newly suspended=1 OR deleted=1 within that month)
Derived from the two series above
mdl_user deactivation count over rolling 12 months, divided by average active headcount for the same period
GREEN <5% Good; AMBER 5-10% Monitor; RED >10% High turnover. High turnover increases training costs for replacements.
New staff without certs - at risk %
COUNT(new hires with zero active documents) / COUNT(all new hires) * 100
mdl_user WHERE timecreated <= NOW()-30d AND no matching sental_document_versions
Above 20% = critical risk for access to hazardous work
Measures exam performance, engagement, subjective course feedback, and completion trend.
Pass Rate, Engagement Ratio, Ratings & Feedback, Completion Trend

Four metrics measuring training effectiveness: first-attempt pass rate per course (sorted worst first), engagement ratio (active time vs. total session time), post-course star rating and NPS, and monthly completion trend per company.

Pass rate below 60% is the configured threshold to flag a course for content review - this threshold must be configurable, not hard-coded. Engagement ratio below 30% (RED) means employees are skipping content to achieve a completion tick without genuinely learning, which voids the compliance value of the certificate and creates legal risk.

Pass rate: passed_on_first_attempt / total_first_attempts * 100 from quiz attempt logs, per course. Engagement: active_time / total_session_time from session activity logs. Rating: AVG(score 1-5) from post-course survey table. NPS: %Promoters - %Detractors from same survey. Sort ascending with configurable reference lines for pass rate (60%) and completion (80%).
Reference line at 60%. Below 60% triggers a recommendation to review course content. Sorted ascending.
Below 3.0 stars flags the course for content review
Range -100 to +100; negative NPS is a strong warning sign
% of respondents rating content as relevant to their job
Used alongside rating/NPS to flag content mismatch
Dashed reference line at 80% target. A falling line is a warning sign.
Quilgo AI proctoring trust scores, by distribution, by company, and cross-referenced with completion rate.
Trust Score Distribution, Average by Company, and Trust-vs-Completion Scatter

Quilgo AI proctoring results: a score distribution across 4 bands (Trusted 90-100 / Review 70-89 / Suspicious 50-69 / Flagged 0-49), average trust score per company, and a scatter plot of completion rate vs. average trust score per course.

The bottom-right quadrant of the scatter (high completion, low trust) is the fraud-detection signal - it identifies courses where employees complete quickly but score poorly on integrity checks, suggesting answer sharing or proxy testing. This is the main integrity control for the entire certification system and must never be hidden by default filters.

Distribution: COUNT(attempts in band) / total_attempts * 100 from Quilgo scores. Scatter: one point per course - X = completion %, Y = AVG(trust_score). Highlight bottom-right quadrant (completion above platform avg AND trust below platform avg) with a warning colour. Join Quilgo API scores to completion logs on course_id and user_id.
Dashed line = platform average. Below-average score combined with high completion % signals possible mass falsification risk.
X = completion %, Y = average trust score
Course completion % cross-referenced with average Quilgo trust score for that course
Bottom-right quadrant (high completion / low trust) = most suspicious; top-right (high completion / high trust) = healthy
Forward-looking document-expiry and training-load projections used for staffing decisions.
30/60/90-Day Mini-Cards, 13-Week Histogram, and 12-Month Training Load Forecast

Three forward-looking views: 30/60/90-day expiry mini-cards (RED/AMBER/BLUE), a 13-week weekly expiry histogram (RED bar when count exceeds peak threshold), and a 12-month stacked training-load forecast across 5 categories.

The histogram turns RED when a week's count exceeds the peak threshold (default 10, slider-adjustable). Ops teams need 2-3 weeks of lead time to schedule retraining. The 12-month load forecast is CEO-only and drives annual staffing and budget decisions - it must clearly distinguish actual vs. projected data.

Expiry counts: COUNT WHERE 0 less than days_to_expiry less than or equal to N from sental_document_versions. 13-week histogram: GROUP BY ISO week. 12-month load: SUM per month of 5 stacked categories - online renewals, offline renewals, new-staff onboarding, document renewals, and EDS workload - from sental_document_versions, enrolment forecasts, and new-hire projections.
Bar turns RED if count >= peak threshold (default 10, adjustable via slider). Plan retraining 2-3 weeks before a peak.
SUM(retraining_online + retraining_offline + new_staff + doc_renewals + EDS) for that month
Combines sental_document_versions (renewals), mdl_user (new staff projections), and course enrolment forecasts
A month is flagged as a "peak period" when its total spikes well above the trailing baseline; example flags 3 peaks with recommended staffing actions (CEO-only view).
Infrastructure health: live capacity gauges, a forward forecast, error counts, and a config status panel.
Capacity Gauges, 90-Day Disk Forecast, Error Log, and System Settings

Five live capacity gauges with 7-day sparklines (click to expand), a 90-day disk forecast via linear regression, a 7-day error count across 6 categories (QR generation, email delivery, EDS rejections, cron overruns, Quilgo API timeouts, file storage), and a system config status panel.

The 90-day forecast gives ops teams advance warning before disk becomes critical. Per-category error counts pinpoint degradation sources without requiring access to raw logs. The config panel flags out-of-date Moodle/PHP versions and misconfigured SMTP before they cause incidents. Threshold values are slider-adjustable - store them in config, never hard-code.

Gauges: same query as KPI drill-down. Forecast: least-squares linear regression over trailing 30 rows from sental_server_metrics history; project to 90 days. Error counts: COUNT per log table (last 7 days). Config: read Moodle/PHP/Cron/Cache/SMTP settings and compare against a stored recommended-values table; flag as OK, Warning, or Check.
Disk / RAM / CPU / Database / Concurrent users (%)
Warning >=70% (adjustable), Critical >=90% (adjustable). Click a gauge for its 7-day sparkline.
~5 weeks to critical at current rate
Linear regression on the trailing 30-day disk-usage history
Critical threshold line at 90% (adjustable); growth rate shown as %/week (example: +0.6%/week)
QR generation failures: 14; Email delivery failures: 7; EDS signature rejections: 3; Cron overruns: 2; Quilgo API timeouts: 0; File storage errors: 0
COUNT(errors in that category within the last 7 days)
sental_qr_log / SMTP send logs / sental_eds_log / mdl_task_log / Quilgo API logs / file storage logs
This is a status read-out, not a calculated KPI - no color threshold, just a raw count with a "last occurred" timestamp.
e.g. Moodle 4.3.2, PHP 8.1.27, Cron running 8 min ago, SMTP 7 failures, log retention unlimited
Direct read of current configuration value vs. a recommended value
Not a calculated formula - a current-vs-recommended config check (example: 6 OK / 2 Warning / 1 Check).

The only tab where the dashboard already implements an automatic pull from system data: clicking "Load from LMS" populates every service quantity from actual training completions for the selected company and month, which the user can then review (and optionally override) before generating the official Excel Act.
Report Configuration - Empty State (before Load from LMS)
The pre-load state of the Act of Completed Works report. Shows 13 service/course rows with blank LMS Count and Act Qty columns - populated only after Load from LMS is clicked.

This is a revenue-critical document and the legal basis for client invoicing. The Load from LMS action must be idempotent (safe to click twice without double-counting). Any discrepancy between LMS Count and Act Qty must be explicitly flagged before download. Generate the Excel server-side to prevent tampering.

On Load from LMS: for each of the 13 rows fire SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sental_completions WHERE status='completed' AND company_id=? AND course_id=? AND MONTH(completed_at)=? AND YEAR(completed_at)=?. Populate LMS Count; default Act Qty = LMS Count. Track any change to Act Qty with the editor identity.
COUNT(sental_completions WHERE status = completed AND company = ? AND course = ? AND month = ? AND year = ?)
sental_completions table, one query per of the 13 service/course line items
Defaults to the LMS Count once loaded; remains user-editable afterward
Same source, then optional manual override before generating the Excel file

The 13 service/course line items are: Industrial Safety at Hazardous Facilities (offline/online), Fire Safety Minimum (offline/online), Occupational Health and Safety (offline/online), Electrical Safety (offline/online), Floor-Operated Crane Operator (offline), Rigger (offline), Working at Heights Safety (offline/online), and Training Coordinator Services. Each gets its own COUNT query with the formula above, filtered to that specific course.
Report Configuration - Loaded State (after Load from LMS) and Derived Stats

The post-load state shows Act Total (SUM of Act Qty), LMS Total (SUM of LMS Count), the difference between them (GREEN if 0, AMBER if non-zero), and a count of rows where Act Qty was manually changed.

The difference counter is an audit control - it makes every manual override visible before the Excel file is sent to the client. A non-zero difference must trigger a confirmation prompt. Modified-row count should be logged with editor identity and timestamp for internal audit.

Act Total = SUM(Act Qty). LMS Total = SUM(LMS Count). Difference = Act Total minus LMS Total. Modified rows = COUNT(rows WHERE Act Qty != LMS Count). Excel export generated client-side from final Act Qty values; includes company name, period, contract number, and service/quantity table in Russian and Kazakh.
SUM(all Act Qty values across the 13 rows)
SUM(all LMS Count values across the 13 rows)
Act Total minus LMS Total. Shown in GREEN if 0, AMBER if not zero.
COUNT(rows where Act Qty does not equal the LMS Count) - flags manual overrides for the reviewer before download

Generated client-side from the final Act Qty values; produces the official multi-language Act of Completed Works document with company, period, contract number, and a service/quantity table matching the on-screen data exactly.
